entities.text: Dr.Kailash Pednekar vs. State of M.P
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Shri Avinash Sirpurkar, learned Senior Counsel with Shri Asif Khan for the applicant.
Shri Amit Singh, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State.

Heard on the admissibility of this criminal revision filed under section 397 read with section 401 of the Cr.P.C against the judgment dated 26.11.2018 delivered by Ist ASJ, Ujjain in criminal revision No.421/2017, by which the judgment pronounced by the JMFC, Ujjain on 24.11.2017 in Criminal Case No.8705/2016 has been partly maintained.
Apart from the hearing on admission, learned Senior Counsel for the applicant also made submissions on IA No.8489/18, which is an application for suspension of sentence.
Both the learned counsel have made elaborate submissions in support of their respective contentions.

Put briefly, the case of the prosecution is that on 19.10.2004 at around 11.00 A.M an inspection was carried out by Food Inspector at the shop of applicant situated at Freeganj, Ujjain, where sealed packets of milk biscuits were kept for being sold.
The Food Inspector purchased the milk biscuits and adopting due procedure, the sample of the biscuits were sent to Public Analyst, State Food Laboratory for examination.
On examination it was found that the biscuits were misbranded as there was no mention of manufacutring date and batch number.
On the basis of the report of the Public Analyst, the applicant was charge sheeted under sections 16(1)(a)(i) & 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

After the prosecution examined the Food Inspector, the trial Court in its judgment dated 24.11.2017 convicted the applicant for misbranding and also for not possessing the license and sentenced to six months simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/-.
The appellate Court in its judgment dated 26.11.2018 acquitted the applicant for committing the offence of misbranding as the applicant was not the manufacturer.

However, he was convicted for selling the biscuits without license and instead of convicting under section 16(1)(a)(i), he was convicted under section 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to 3 months RI with fine of Rs.500/- and in default of fine further to undergo RI for ten days.

During arguments, learned Senior Counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant has already suffered imprisonment since 26.11.2018 and has faced prosecution for 13 years and looking to his detention in jail as already suffered by him to be considered appropriate sentence and in that case he would not be inclined to press IA No.8489/18 for suspension of sentence.
Considered.

sentences.text: The original record of the case was perused along with the evidence of witness.
Also considered in entirety the judgment of the trial Court as well as appellate Court.
This apart, learned counsel for the applicant made an admission on behalf of the applicant that he did not possess the requisite license for selling the packets of biscuits which were seized.
In view of this admission as well as after considering the evidence on record, it is found proved that applicant did not possess the requisite license to sell the biscuits which were seized.
Consequently, the conviction of the applicant under section 16(1)(a)(ii) of the PFA Act is maintained.

However, considering the question of sentence, I am of the opinion that ends of justice would be served if the jail sentence of applicant is reduced to the period already undergone by him in jail and the fine amount is increased from Rs.500/- to Rs.3,000/-.

Consequently, it is ordered that on depositing the additional fine amount of Rs.2500/-
by the applicant, he shall be released forthwith, if not required in any other offence.
On failure to pay the fine amount, the substantive sentence of 3 months RI shall prevail.

In the result, the revision petition is allowed in part and IA No.8489/18 stands disposed of.
C.c as per rules.
(SHAILENDRA SHUKLA) JUDGE Date: 2018.12.19 09:14:57 -08'00' hk/
